CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.title: Pointwise decay bound at local points, equal-types case
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.summary: For any real constants Cb, C₃ ≥ 0, CΛ ≥ 0, C₀ ≥ 1/2 there are constants C₄, c₃, Cc, Cc', Cc'' such that the following holds for every parameter record P (with integers k, r), every pair of finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces, every 'place' datum p, operator-valued function f on a matrix space, base b ≥ 3, shift n₀ with shift data S (which supplies two shifted places). Assume a list of numerical side conditions (sizes of Λ, n₀, p₀, K, N, and four lower bounds on a decay exponent A₀), smoothness and decay of f, a derivative expansion on the big cell, and for both shifted places the existence of 'wave grids' and 'lift grids' and a limit bound. Then `ThmBpAt` holds: at every local point γ with G(γ) > 0, the quantity E(γ) attached to f is at most b^(C₄(2r+2)⁴) · G(γ)^(−(2p₀+n₀)) times a norm of f.
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.role: Bookkeeping: it is `thmBpAt_eqR_top` from `NormalFormTopDomination` with two extra hypotheses (membership of two auxiliary functions in a function class) added and ignored, so that it matches the packaged statement `AsmEq`. CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.caveat: The statement is a long inequality in the project's `HermitianCurvature` machinery; the meaning of a place datum, of the quantities E and G, of the grids and of the limit bound was not unfolded. 'Equal types' comes from the theorem name and the `CutBPEq` namespace, not from a definition that was read.

literature.basis: The inequality is phrased entirely in the project's own structures (place data, wave grids, lift grids, shift data) and carries no literature naming, but its mathematical content was not unfolded far enough to tell whether it corresponds to a known decay estimate.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Level subgroups act by characters on the finite datum

Hypotheses: the chain data are admissible (`I.Ok`, `TC.Pins`) and the pinning conditions `PinX` and `PinColL` hold; these say, among other things, that the additive character is standard, the vacuum functions are the vacuum vectors of the integral lattices, `kom j` is a Weil datum for the character, and the combination built from `dd` is the prescribed rational theta datum. Conclusion: for every step j < m, every pair of live chart classes and every pair of elements k of U_j and k' of U_{j+1}, the operator `kom j (k, k')` multiplies the vector obtained as the finite combination of Heisenberg translates of the vacuum function by the scalar χ_j(k)^(-1) · χ_{j+1}(k'). Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Bounds for degenerate terms and collision terms, unconditional
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: No hypotheses. Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Diagonal Gram bound from the unitary Siegel–Weil formula
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypothesis: the Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups in the convergent range, for every CM extension E/F and every non-degenerate Hermitian form of size M (the adelic quotient has finite volume, and for 2n < M the average of the theta series over vectors with a given non-degenerate n×n Gram matrix equals an archimedean density times a convergent product of local densities). Conclusion: a uniform 'diagonal row' bound. For any auxiliary constants there are thresholds and a constant C ≥ 1 such that, for every datum `D` produced by the project's construction, every scale L and every index u, if the scale condition `IsScaleWithBoundedGamma`, the rank identity `RankMu` (for all indices) and the standing hypothesis bundle `HD` hold, then the squared Hilbert–Schmidt distance from the identity of the normalized Gram operator on the finite-dimensional space attached to u is at most 4(exp(C·m^5·f·L) + 1)·d²/D* + (4·exp(−k·f·log k / 2) + 2·exp(−k·f·log k))·d, where d is the dimension of that space.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Transformation law of the kernel function ξ under level groups
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Setting: the project's column datum I (with its conditions `Ok` and `Pins`), the global datum built from it, and a 'twisted datum' A satisfying the bundle `A.Is` (about a dozen conditions tying level charts, base points, characters χ, a Hecke-type character chr and an idempotent e of the adelic algebra). For consecutive Hermitian spaces X_i and X_(i+1) of the chain, ξ is a complex-valued function on matrices over E attached to two chart indices. Assume ξ is unchanged when the e-projection of its argument changes by k times an e-fixed element of the standard integral lattice (k a positive integer). Let κ, κ' be elements of the level groups U_i and U_(i+1) whose components at the primes in the set Q(a) are matrices over E, with determinant roots x and y. If acting by (κ, κ') inverse on the e-projection of z gives the e-projection of z' plus k times such a lattice element, then chr(x)⁻¹ · chr(y) · ξ(z') = χ_i(κ)⁻¹ · χ_(i+1)(κ') · ξ(z).

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Arithmetic Kleiman and Hilbert–Samuel bounds from three inputs

Then three results hold for such arithmetic varieties and Hermitian line bundles: an arithmetic Kleiman-type theorem (a relatively semipositive, fibrewise nef, conjugation-invariant bundle with non-negative degree on all one-dimensional arithmetic subvarieties has non-negative top arithmetic self-intersection); and two arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel upper bounds (the limsup of the log-number of small integral sections of the n-th power, divided by n^(D+1)/(D+1)!, is at most the arithmetic self-intersection number), one for 'small generated' data and one for semipositive bundles with bounded monomials.

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Arithmetic nefness and Hilbert–Samuel upper bounds, unconditionally
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.summary: The statement `HSUse` is proved with no hypotheses. Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Nadel vanishing for pairs and isolated non-klt divisors
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.summary: A conjunction of two statements about a normal integral projective scheme X of dimension n over the complex numbers. (2) Isolating a non-klt point: if (X, Δ) is klt, x is a closed point, N₀ is nef and big, and positive numbers c(1..n) satisfy c(e)^e < (N₀^e · Z)/r^e for every irreducible e-dimensional subvariety Z through x together with the sum of e/c(e) over e = 1..n being at most 1, then there is an effective Cartier divisor D₀ and m > 0 with D₀/m numerically equivalent to N₀/r such that (X, Δ + D₀/m) is log canonical near x, klt near x away from x, and not klt at x.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Siegel–Weil coefficient identity for singular Hermitian matrices
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: Setting: a Hermitian space V of rank n over the CM field E of the project's datum, an integer r with 2r < n, a nontrivial additive character of the adeles of F, self-dual-type Haar measures (covolume one) on adelic n × r matrices and on adelic Hermitian r × r matrices, a Haar measure on the adelic unitary group of V, and an adelic Schwartz function φ on V^r whose theta integral converges absolutely. The companion statement `SiegelND` covers nonsingular β.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Siegel–Weil Euler product for singular block-form Gram matrices
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: Let E/F be a CM extension of number fields with conjugation σ, J a non-degenerate Hermitian matrix of size M over E, and T an n-by-n Hermitian matrix that is zero outside an invertible upper-left t-by-t block with t < n (so T is singular). Then the project's property `SWFree` holds: for standard Haar measures and any fundamental domain for the rational points of the unitary group of J in its adelic points, the normalised average over that domain of the translates of all rational linearly independent tuples with Gram matrix T is an Euler product, with constant 1, of the local fibre measures of the Gram map over T at the archimedean places and at each finite place.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Covolume of the adelic unitary quotient equals the standard mass
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: Let D be the project's global datum (it supplies a CM field E over its totally real subfield F), and V a Hermitian space over E with a unimodular base lattice whose signature is the same pair (P, Q) at every complex embedding. Take any Haar measure μ on the adelic unitary group of V, any fundamental domain 𝓕 for its rational points, Haar measures m on the real groups U(P, Q) normalised by a fixed density at the identity, and a continuous homomorphism rp to the product of these real groups that reads off the archimedean components in given frames. Then for every measurable set B in the product, μ(𝓕) · m(B) = μ{h : h stabilises the adelic base lattice and rp(h) ∈ B} · volU(n)^f · mass, where n is the rank, f the degree of F, volU(n) an explicit constant, and mass is the mass (sum of reciprocals of automorphism-group orders over the genus) of the standard positive definite unimodular Hermitian lattice of rank n. In words: the covolume of the rational points, measured against the lattice stabiliser, does not depend on the signature and equals the definite mass.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.role: Assembled in the same file from the lemma `pi_cd_eq_map` (the product of the compact-dual-normalised real measures is the pushforward of the restricted adelic measure), the project's volume tie for the datum (`retie_volTieG_and_cdScaleTie`), the identity `vol_eq_massI_all_sig` (volume equals rank mass for all signatures) and a rescaling between two normalisations of Haar measure on U(P, Q). It is a volume identity later used for the upper and lower Tamagawa-type bounds (`up`, `low`).

Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.title: Theta integrals of two unitary dual pairs agree
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.summary: Hypotheses: fourteen named propositions, among them a Siegel-set statement for unitary groups from the `Published` folder, a Siegel-Weil statement, meromorphic continuation of Eisenstein series, existence of Weil representations, a ramified multiplicity-one statement, finite-place statements at ramified, split and inert places, a spherical statement, two archimedean Lie-algebra statements, existence of archimedean matching maps, and two implications about coinvariants. Setting of the conclusion: a CM-type extension E/F of number fields, Hermitian spaces V of rank a and V' of rank a' < a and a skew-Hermitian space W of rank a + a', two Hecke characters alpha and beta, and Weil representations for the pairs (U(V), U(W)) and (U(V'), U(W)). Conclusion 1 (`ThetaIntegralsAgree`): the theta integrals converge with moderate growth; for any matched local data there is a unique constant c, and it is non-zero, such that the theta integral over U(V) of a function equals c times the theta integral over U(V') of every matching function; the finite-place maps are coinvariant quotients at good places; and there are universal signs such that when a hyperbolic plane is removed from V or from V' the constants change by an explicit factor made of ideal-character values, local epsilon factors and a value of the partial Hecke L-function of alpha/beta. Conclusion 2 (`LocalMatching`): matched local data always exist.
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.role: Final assembly for this block: about 150 intermediate statements are derived one by one from the hypotheses and from unconditional project lemmas, collected into the bundle `ThKG.Leaves`, and passed to `agree_of_leaves`. The second component comes from existence of the archimedean and finite matching maps.
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.caveat: Only the head and tail of the proof were read. The matching relation (`Match`, `PolMatch`), the local map structures (`RealMaps`, `FinMaps`) and several hypotheses (`FinRam`, `SphTri`, `LieSecond`) were read as definitions but not fully unfolded; which hypotheses are literature statements is judged from names and folders.

literature.basis: The comparison is in the tradition of Siegel-Weil and Rallis, but the statement is about the project's own matching data and constants and is conditional on named hypotheses, so it is not a restatement of a published theorem.

Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.title: Comparison of theta integrals for two unitary dual pairs (conditional)
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.summary: Seven hypotheses are assumed: Bernstein's theorem that the parabolically induced product of two irreducible unitarisable smooth representations of p-adic general linear groups is irreducible; `SiegelCore` (reduction theory for adelic unitary groups over CM extensions: Siegel sets, Iwasawa decomposition, rapid decay of cusp forms); `EisBL` (convergence and meromorphic continuation of Siegel Eisenstein series on doubled unitary groups); `SiegelWeilStd` (the Siegel–Weil formula for a definite unitary group paired with a doubled one); and three local statements at finite places for the Weil representations in a 'triple' (`SphSplit` at split places, `HoweInert` and `SphFun` at non-split places, about spherical vectors, Howe's generation property for the vacuum vector, and equality of spherical functionals). Conclusion: `ThetaIntegralsAgree` and `LocalMatching`. For a CM extension E/F, Hermitian spaces V (dimension a) and V' (dimension a' < a) and a skew-Hermitian space W of dimension a + a' with compatible Hecke characters, matching data exist at the real and finite places; the theta integrals over the unitary group of V and over that of V' converge, and for matching Schwartz functions they agree up to one nonzero constant which is unique; two recursion steps relate these constants when a hyperbolic plane is removed, with an explicit factor containing a partial Hecke L-value and local epsilon factors.
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.role: Final assembly of the project's 'Theorem K' in its spherical form: it calls `Tr.closeSph` with facts derived from Bernstein's theorem (coinvariants, multiplicity one at ramified and split places), the three local hypotheses, project-proved archimedean facts and the Siegel-domain, Eisenstein and Siegel–Weil inputs.
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.caveat: The conclusion's definitions (`IsTriple`, `Match`, `IsConst`, `StepAlpha`, `StepBeta`) were read; the real and finite 'matching maps' (`IsRealMaps`, `IsFinMaps`) and the internals of the proof term `closeSph` were not unfolded. The label 'Theorem K' comes from the theorem name.

literature.basis: Several hypotheses are literature statements (Bernstein's irreducibility theorem is in the project's `Published` namespace; the Siegel–Weil formula and Eisenstein continuation are classical), but the conclusion is an identity between theta integrals with project-specific matching data and normalisations, which I could not identify with a named published theorem.

Formalism.LocalToGlobal.SiegelLatticeThe.title: Kernel expansion holds in every tied concrete setting

GlobalTheory.BigOn.ontoX_of_hypotheses_a.title: The 'onto' inequality at family points from twelve published inputs

GlobalTheory.ConjClassSum.conj_lifts.title: Theta lifts of Galois-conjugate data have conjugate cusp-form expansions
GlobalTheory.ConjClassSum.conj_lifts.summary: Setting: the project's data type D with a family of characters indexed by tuples t in a finite set, real data R, a face F, weights κ, vectors v₀, 'one-map' data O, phases ph, and an index i. GlobalTheory.T.hasSemiAbelianUniformisat.title: Mumford-type uniformisation from degeneration data over complete normal base
GlobalTheory.T.hasSemiAbelianUniformisat.summary: Let R be a local domain that is noetherian, integrally closed, complete for its maximal ideal, and of characteristic zero. Let D be degeneration data over R relative to the maximal ideal: a polarized abelian scheme over R with a rigidified, cubical, symmetric line bundle, a free abelian group X of finite rank mapping additively to its points, and trivialisations ψ(χ) of the pulled-back inverse line bundle at the generic point, with ψ even, the associated τ bimultiplicative, ψ(χ) lying in the maximal ideal for χ ≠ 0, and ψ(χ) lying in the n-th power of the maximal ideal for all but finitely many χ. Then there exist a commutative group scheme G over Spec R that is semi-abelian and a polarized abelian variety A over the fraction field such that G is uniformised by D: G is smooth and separated with generic fibre A, compatibly with line bundles, its reductions modulo powers of the maximal ideal are related to the abelian part and the torus with character group X, and sections of powers of the line bundle correspond bijectively to theta-type expansions.
GlobalTheory.T.hasSemiAbelianUniformisat.role: A restatement under the project's theorem namespace of `GlobalTheory.Mum.has_of_base`. That proof reduces the data to a factor of unitary PEL type, passes to a finite extension carrying a labelled cover, obtains the uniformisation there, descends along the finite extension, and cuts out the required factor by an idempotent.
GlobalTheory.T.hasSemiAbelianUniformisat.caveat: `Base`, `AdmBase`, `Has`, `DegPre`, `DegData` and the first fields of `UnifPre` were read; the remaining fields of the uniformisation structure (compatibilities at each thickening and the expansion bijection `ExpBij`) were only skimmed, and `IsSemiAbelian`, `PolAV`, `CubicalStr` were taken at face value.

literature.basis: The statement has the form of Mumford's construction of degenerating abelian varieties over a complete normal base (Mumford 1972; Faltings–Chai, Chapter III), and the project's namespace `Mum` points to it; the exact packaging of 'uniformised' is the project's own, so the match is not verified in detail.

GlobalTheory.T.volume_theorem_of_inputs.title: Volume theorem for towers over unitary moduli, from ten inputs
GlobalTheory.T.volume_theorem_of_inputs.summary: Hypotheses: ten propositions: a large bundle `Given` (toroidal level and Hecke compatibilities, a key formula, extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes, a Fargues Hodge–Tate statement, GAGA for sections, a slope bound, and other inputs), integrability of fibre sums of point densities, the properties of the Weil pairing on torsion of polarized abelian schemes, existence of two constants Ch, Cu for a nine-part geometric statement, a Hodge lattice flag bound, triviality of a flag on the Hodge bundle, a flat degree statement, a twisting automorphism statement, and two comparison statements. Conclusion `VolumeTheoremX`: there is a constant C ≥ 0 such that for every abelian CM field E, every unitary-type moduli datum of signature (p, q) with q ≥ 1 and 3q + 1 ≤ p + q, every integral model Y, every 'root tower' T over it with a good origin, and every full intersection system, if the tower has at most 4·|CM type|·(p+q)² bad primes, then: geometric degrees on each component are a positive volume times flag-variety degrees and do not depend on the level B; all components have the same volume; certain top arithmetic intersection numbers and their ratios to degrees converge as a parameter s tends to 0; an asymptotic formula for arithmetic intersection numbers holds with error O(log B / B); and the arithmetic intersection number and the mean slope over components are bounded below by −C times an explicit bracket term.
GlobalTheory.T.volume_theorem_of_inputs.role: A restatement under the project's theorem namespace of `volumeTheoremX_of_inputs`, which is a long assembly: it takes the constant 2·max(Ch + Cu/2, 0) + 17 and derives each conjunct from earlier 'good tower' and 'real tower' results (proportionality, nefness, intersection identities, a power-sum relation) together with the listed inputs.
GlobalTheory.T.volume_theorem_of_inputs.caveat: `VolumeTheoremX`, `Proportional`, `VolEq`, `T1`, `ThmB`, `T2`, `MeanSlope`, `Given`, `WeilSt` and `PtsIntegrableStatement` were read; `RootTower`, `GoodOrigin`, `IntersectionSystem`, the bracket term and the remaining seven hypotheses were not unfolded, so the geometric interpretation (arithmetic intersection numbers, slopes) rests partly on names of fields such as `PP`, `slope`, `volT`.

literature.basis: The conclusion concerns root towers and good origins defined in this project and gives a new-looking uniform lower bound; the proportionality part resembles Hirzebruch–Mumford proportionality but the statement as a whole has no literature marker.

Main.title: Zeros of primitive Dirichlet L-functions lie on the critical line
Main.summary: For every modulus N ≥ 1 and every primitive Dirichlet character χ modulo N, if s is a complex number with 0 < Re s < 1 and the (Mathlib) L-function of χ vanishes at s, then Re s = 1/2. There are no other hypotheses. The same file states four companion results before this one: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`, the project's own wording of it for the zeta function, non-vanishing of every Dirichlet L-function for Re s > 1/2 (away from the pole of the trivial character at s = 1), and the critical-line statement for all Dirichlet characters.
Main.role: Top-level final statement. It is a one-line restatement of `critAll`, which is obtained in `Supplements.Kernels.MainTheorems` from `allChi` (non-vanishing of all Dirichlet L-functions to the right of 1/2, i.e. `UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter`) through `Formalism.VW.critLine`.
Main.caveat: Only the statement, its definition in `Statements.lean` and the one-step proof terms were read; the chain of results behind `allChi` was not examined here.

literature.basis: The statement is the generalised Riemann hypothesis for primitive Dirichlet L-functions (and the file also concludes RH itself); no accepted proof of either existed in the literature.

UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter.title: Non-vanishing of all Dirichlet L-functions from a Galois-representation hypothesis
UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter.summary: Hypothesis `Row0b`: for every CM field E, prime l, isomorphism of the algebraic closure of Q_l with C, and every regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_a over E that is polarized by a Hecke character of the maximal real subfield, there is a continuous semisimple a-dimensional l-adic representation of the Galois group of E with prescribed Hodge–Tate weights, compatible with π at places away from l in a weakened sense (equal dimension, equality in the toral case, matching characteristic polynomials on inertia-degree-zero elements in a tame case) and crystalline or de Rham / potentially semistable above l; compatibility is measured against any local map satisfying the project's local-Langlands laws. Conclusion: for every modulus N ≥ 1, every Dirichlet character χ mod N and every s with Re s > 1/2 (excluding s = 1 when χ is trivial), L(χ, s) ≠ 0.
UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter.role: A reduction of the main theorem to one input. The hypothesis is used twice to fill the three-field bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements` (the middle field, existence of a local reciprocity map, is supplied by a theorem of the project), then `every_character_of_literature_of_vWin` is applied with the condition `VWin` obtained from the same hypothesis by `vwin_of_row`. The next declaration in the file discharges the hypothesis and deduces RH.
UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter.caveat: The fine conditions inside `Row0b` (the predicates for crystalline, de Rham, tame, and the Weil–Deligne comparison) were not unfolded beyond their names. `VWin` (a bound on sums of lengths of Tate–Shafarevich-type groups over fields cut out by χ) was read but its role in the proof was not followed.

literature.basis: The conclusion is the generalised Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions in non-vanishing form, which had no proof; the hypothesis itself resembles known theorems on Galois representations of polarized automorphic representations (Harris–Taylor, Shin, Chenevier–Harris, Caraiani).

UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.title: Bundle of twenty-eight published arithmetic-geometry theorems
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.summary: Hypothesis: the three-field bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements` (existence of Galois representations for polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representations over CM fields, stated twice, and existence of a local reciprocity map for GL_n). Conclusion: the structure `PublishedHodgeBundleTheorems`, whose 28 fields are propositions from the project's `Published` list: toroidal compactification, arithmetic volume lower bound and nef volume, an Arakelov calculus statement, de Rham cohomology of abelian schemes, ray class fields, semistable reduction, strong approximation for special unitary groups, a Green series statement, good Chern–Weil forms, Landherr's theorem on Hermitian forms, the Hasse norm theorem for quadratic extensions, extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes, a lowest-alcove statement for induced modules, a section for principal polarisations, the count n^(2g) of n-torsion points of an abelian variety, Grothendieck–Messing, prismatic Dieudonné theory, Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing, nef numerics, L² extension, arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel, existence of Chow forms, heights of cycles, Serre's holomorphic sections, Nadel vanishing, principalisation, and formal algebraisation.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.role: Bookkeeping: each field is filled by a one-line lemma of the same file. A textual check of the file indicates that none of these 28 lemmas actually uses the hypothesis; each refers to a result proved elsewhere in the project (for example strong approximation, Landherr, toroidal compactification are cited as outright theorems).
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.caveat: Seven of the 28 field propositions were opened (Kawamata–Viehweg, Hasse norm, Landherr, strong approximation, n-torsion count, arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel, volume bound) and match the theorems they are named after; the remaining fields are described from their names. That the hypothesis is unused was checked by pattern matching within this file, not by the Lean kernel.

literature.basis: Every field lives in the project's `Published` namespace and those inspected restate standard theorems; the declaration only packages them. The exact Lean formulations are project-specific, so a full match with the literature was not verified for all fields.
